whyTheseWords: `granted` is unchanged, so the claim a prospect already read does not silently change meaning, and the Connections register's separate product-wide `1 of 12 sources connected` keeps its own verb.

`demonstrated with fixture records` reuses the chrome's own shipped vocabulary - web/index.html already carries `Generated fixture`, `generated fixture records` and `Demo records` - rather than inventing a fifth word for the same thing.

Same denominator, 10, on both figures, because both count DISTINCT ADAPTER KINDS out of the same catalog. Comparable units are what makes the two numbers legible side by side; a regions-populated numerator (3) against a kinds denominator (10) would be a ratio with two counting rules.
Both figures carry a denominator inline (DEV_PROCESS 1.1) and each carries its own counting rule at the point of use (DEV_PROCESS 1.2).

The demonstrated RULE branches on the pack rather than the label, so a pack that generates nothing states the positive determination `this pack generates no records` instead of leaving a bare 0 (AGENT_CONTRACT s5: an empty result is not an absence).

derivation.where: src/city-identity.mjs packSources(), the SAME resolver that already derives the granted figure. One resolver, so there is nothing to diverge (DEV_PROCESS 2.4).

derivation.hardcodedAnywhere: no. The proof required by the dispatch is a scratch-copy run that moves the catalog and the grants and watches both numbers move with no source edit; it lands in CP2.
derivation.neonPath: packSources will read pack.fixtureGrants and pack.generatesFixtures. Both are already in PACK_COLUMNS (fixture_grants, generates_fixtures), and city-identity.test.mjs's structural guard - every pack property city-identity.mjs reads must be a column the SELECT names - covers the new reads automatically.

bakeDiscipline.reBake: node scripts/bake-connections.mjs, then `G-88 the bake is fresh / leaves web/index.html unchanged when the bake is run again` must be green. The dispatch's own named test is the proof, and CP2/close carry it watched FAILING on a planted hand edit.
bakeDiscipline.handTypedCountsFound: web/index.html carries `67 of 67 | Homes-table row` and `3 | layout-inventory addendum` in the Connections panel head, plus a t-caption restating the counting rule in prose. NONE of the three is baked today - they are hand-typed copies of a rule that lives in src/shell-homes.mjs. That is the drift shape this repo has already paid for twice (`7 integrations`, `0 of 4`). PROPOSAL: give them ids and bake them from the register, so the fixed-point test covers them and no future split can leave a stale count on the page.
bakeDiscipline.scopeJustification: this is not scope creep away from G-93; it is the only way the new count can be stated on the page without hand-typing it, which the dispatch forbids for the footer figure and which would be no more defensible here.

adversarialReview: RISK: splitting changes SHELL_HOMES.length, and src/shell-homes.test.mjs pins 67 and the per-table breakdown, and src/server.test.mjs:288-289 pins `/67 of 67/` and 70 baked rows over the SERVED document. Both move with the rule, and both keep a per-table assertion so a split cannot hide in a total.

RISK: `splitFrom` is a new field that nothing enforces, so a future split could omit it and the source-row count would silently rise. MITIGATED: a test asserts every splitFrom value names a job that is NOT itself a register row, and that every split group has more than one member - so a stray or self-referential splitFrom fails rather than resolving quietly.

RISK: calling Feedback `Mounted` while this deployment cannot deliver. CHECKED: Mounted is used in this register for surfaces that are mounted (Reviewer queue, Citizen service requests), not for surfaces whose dependencies are configured; and the composer reports the destination's real answer rather than a fabricated success, so the mounted claim is true independent of configuration.

RISK: `Empty` for Notifications could be read as `no notifications exist` rather than `no source can raise one`. MITIGATED: the home text carries the nuance, which is what the file's own header comment says the home column is for.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: move the nuance into the home text and set the disposition from the unbuilt leg, which is the other option the G-90 lane offered. It keeps 67 and needs no counting-rule change, but it makes the register's disposition column report the WORST leg of a bundle rather than the state of a job - so the built theme toggle and the built notifications tray would both read `Not built` on the page whose entire purpose is to be the honest build map.
